audit.why: A ranged AP laner who loses every extended melee exchange from 3 onward and converts to a pick threat late — consistent with 51.3% over 1,195 games.
audit.corrected: Kept; the two mechanics that decide the lane were added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike treated Pop Blossom as a plain telegraphed ult you can dash out of.
audit.why: Riot's text: "The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised." Advice to "save E to dash out of the wind-up" is actively dangerous against a disguised Neeko, because there is no wind-up to react to.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] and mid now state the hidden wind-up and give the disguise as the real tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two kit rules that change how you take the trade were absent.
audit.why: Blooming Burst "blooms again on hitting champions or killing units" — it is a double hit, not a single, and it is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s. Tangle-Barbs "becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer" after passing through a champion or killing a unit, so standing behind a dying minion makes her root strictly better.
audit.corrected: early states both rules; mid and wants.you[0] give the 9s trade window.

edits.before: Neeko out-ranges you at Level 1 with Blooming Burst (Q), a hop-detonating AoE that chunks you before you have a Q pattern or E lifesteal to fight back. Don't walk into the second bloom for CS, and respect that her E (Tangle-Barbs) roots — that root is what sets up her all-in. Farm safely and dodge her Q at level 1; by level 2 your emerging damage lets you start pressuring back and pull ahead. Even at 1 because she has range but no kill pressure on a healthy Aatrox — then you edge in front.
edits.after: Neeko out-ranges you at level 1 with Blooming Burst (Q), a seed that blooms again on hitting a champion, so it chunks you twice over before you have a Q pattern or E lifesteal to fight back. Don't stand in the second bloom for CS, and respect Tangle-Barbs (E) — its root lasts longer and the tangle flies faster once it has passed through a champion or killed a unit, so never eat it from behind a dying minion. Farm safely and dodge her Q at level 1; by level 2 your emerging damage lets you pressure back and pull ahead.

edits.before: From Level 3-6 the fight tilts hard to you. You gap-close with E, chain W to hold her still, and land Q3 sweetspot — one full combo plus drain erases her poke and threatens a kill. Her Blooming Burst on cooldown is a big window with no wave-clear detonation; force trades then. At 6, respect Pop Blossom's stun-burst, but World Ender's heal amp means you tank it and win the exchange, especially if you E out of the tell.
edits.after: From level 3-6 the fight tilts hard to you. You gap-close with E, chain W to hold her still, and land Q3 sweetspot — one combo plus drain erases her poke and threatens a kill. Blooming Burst is 9s at rank 1; with it down she has no wave-clear detonation, so force trades then. At 6, respect Pop Blossom — and know its wind-up is HIDDEN while she is disguised, so an approaching "ally" is the tell.

edits.before: Bait your combo with a clone or disguise, then burst
edits.after: Hide the Pop Blossom wind-up in a disguise, then burst

edits.before: Dodge Blooming Burst (Q) then commit with E and Q pattern
edits.after: Trade in the 9s window after Blooming Burst is spent

edits.before: Her ult (Pop Blossom) is a hard stun-burst, but World Ender's heal amp lets you survive it and win the follow-up; save E to dash out of the wind-up if you can.
edits.after: Pop Blossom knocks up then stuns, but World Ender lets you survive it and win the follow-up; save E for the wind-up — unless she is disguised, when there is none.

notes: Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag Riot's description does not support (drag + slow only); no grounding claim was made in this slice.
